Build on the same branch as setup-turns-off-for-a-project-the-plugins-it-doe (same file). IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen).
Also: bin/relay the setup flags (--no-global, --global) and the usage text
Also: lib/relay_setup.py the doctor checks of the relay marketplace

details: CONFIRMED by reading. The design's fact at line 35-37 ("the blocks merge_bindings adds ... are exactly relay_defaults()")
holds only for flow "none": the [flow] block is `kind = "{flow}"`, and flow is "issues" whenever the run says --flow issues
or detect() finds issue skills, an [issues] section or .issues/. Section 4's rule "add a section only when its value is
not what a missing section means" is right; line 108 applies it wrongly to [flow]. The fix stays inside the design: add
[flow] when the chosen flow is not "none". Size: 5 minutes in the design, 15 in the build (one test).
evidence: plugins/core/hooks/flow-stage.py:45-48   name = cfg.get("flow", {}).get("kind"); if name not in ("", "none"): bind it
failing_case: A project with .claude/kit.toml holding only [project] and [gate] (no [flow], no [issues], no .issues/), run
`relay setup <dir> --flow issues`.
Today: merge_bindings appends `[flow] kind = "issues"` (lib/relay_setup.py:251 builds the block from `flow`), so
plugins/core/hooks/flow-stage.py:45 reads kind "issues" and the issue stages fire.
Under the design (section 4, line 108: "[flow] ... never added (they equal relay_defaults())"): nothing is added,
issues@relay is set true, but flow-stage.py finds no [flow] kind and binds nothing; doctor (relay_setup.py:1015) reports
"flow bound (none)" and skips the issue flow's bindings_required check. The issue flow is silently off.
Should: `[flow] kind = "issues"` is written, as today.
fix_hint: Section 4: "[flow]: added when the chosen flow is not "none"; [delegate], [observe]: never added." Add the test case of
pass_cases: 1. kit.toml without [flow], `--flow issues` -> kit.toml gains `[flow]\nkind = "issues"`; issues@relay true.
2. kit.toml without [flow], no --flow, nothing detected -> no [flow] added (the design's intent; T11 first part).
3. kit.toml without [flow], `--flow none` -> no [flow] added (the value is the default).
4. Relay tree (T1) -> kit.toml byte-identical.
reason: Carried from the earlier check of 5ecc184 (MET there); the only change since is the t22 test rewrite 8739ae9, and tests/test_setup_off.py passes (73 passed with test_setup.py).
findings.summary: never adding [flow] to an existing kit.toml drops `relay setup --flow issues`: the issues plugin is on but the flow-stage hook binds nothing

details: CONFIRMED by the probe. The new FIX exists to protect the merge hook (design line 138-139: "This is the protection the
relay-plugins item exists for"); a local-scope disable is exactly the case a person reaches with Claude Code's own
command, and it is invisible in git. The fix stays inside the design: "actually on" = local value, else project, else
user, else off. Setup itself must not write settings.local.json (it is the person's own). Size: 5 minutes design, 15 build.
evidence: cd <scratch> (settings.json observe@relay true, settings.local.json observe@relay false); claude plugin list --json
claude plugin disable --help: -s, --scope <scope>  Installation scope: user, project, local
failing_case: Project .claude/settings.json: `core@relay: true`; .claude/settings.local.json: `core@relay: false` (what
`claude plugin disable core@relay --scope local` writes). Claude Code shows the plugin disabled; the merge hook and the
main-checkout guard do not run. The design's doctor (line 20, line 136-137) reads the project value true and passes.
Should: FIX "core@relay is off for this project ...".
Probe, 26 Oct, scratch folder: project settings observe@relay true + settings.local.json observe@relay false ->
`claude plugin list --json` shows observe@relay enabled False; the same folder without the local file -> enabled True.
fix_hint: Line 20 and section 6: define "actually on" as settings.local.json, else settings.json, else user settings, else off;
pass_cases: 1. local false, project true, user true -> doctor FIX for that plugin.
2. local true, project false -> passes (local wins).
3. no local file, project false, user true -> FIX (T12 first part).
4. no local file, no project key, user true -> passes (T12 second part).
5. The same rule feeds the spec check (T14): local openspec@relay true, [specs] none -> FIX.
reason: Carried from the earlier check of 5ecc184 (MET there); the only change since is the t22 test rewrite 8739ae9, and tests/test_setup_off.py passes (73 passed with test_setup.py).
findings.summary: doctor's 'actually on' (project, else user, else off) ignores .claude/settings.local.json, which beats the project file

details: CONFIRMED by reading the design against the rename item, whose Why says the rename must move settings "so no project
silently loses the merge hook". The brief says this design "must not make that rename harder"; deriving false from the
marketplace while the true set stays a separate literal (three copies: relay_plugins_for line 305, USER_SCOPE_PLUGINS
line 608, merge_user_settings callers 742/1147, plus doctor 967) turns a missed literal from harmless into a silent
off. The same holds for any plugin added to the marketplace later and turned on at user scope only: the next setup run
writes it false in every project. Fix inside the design: one always-on tuple used by all of them, and setup refuses
when an always-on name is not in marketplace.json (fact to code, principle 5). Size: 15 design, 30 build.
evidence: design line 70-78 (table over marketplace plugins, row 5 "no key -> false"); line 150-152 (literals stay for the rename);
design T15: "Fixture marketplace.json named amidman (same plugin names)".
queue the-core-plugin-becomes-relay-amidman: "plugin ids become relay@amidman, ..." "so no project silently loses the merge hook"
failing_case: The planned rename (queue item the-core-plugin-becomes-relay-amidman) renames plugin core to relay and the marketplace
to amidman. Suppose marketplace.json is updated and relay_plugins_for's literal list (lib/relay_setup.py:305, which the
design keeps, line 150-152) still says "core". The design's table iterates marketplace.json: p = "relay" is not in
{core, observe, delegate, front}, no key exists after [plugin_key] deletes core@relay, so row 5 writes
`relay@amidman: false` into every project file. A project false beats the user true (the design's own probe), so the
merge checks and the guard stop in every project set up again. Today (no false lines) the same miss leaves a dangling
`core@amidman: true` and the user-scope plugin keeps running.
T15 does not catch it: its fixture keeps "the same plugin names".
Should: setup never writes false for an always-on plugin; a name mismatch is refused before any write.
fix_hint: Section 2/7: name one always-on tuple (e.g. USER_SCOPE_PLUGINS) that relay_plugins_for, merge_user_settings and doctor
read; table row 0: "p is always-on -> true, never false"; a check before any write that every always-on name is in
marketplace.json. Add pass-case 1 as a test next to T15.
pass_cases: 1. Fixture marketplace.json with "relay" in place of "core", always-on list still naming "core" -> setup raises
ValueError naming the missing always-on plugin; settings.json unchanged (bytes and mtime).
2. Fixture marketplace.json with names matching the always-on list (T15) -> every key ends @amidman, none ends @relay.
3. Relay tree (T1) -> as T1.
4. A test reads marketplace.json and asserts every always-on name is a plugin name in it.
reason: Carried from the earlier check of 5ecc184 (MET there); the only change since is the t22 test rewrite 8739ae9, and tests/test_setup_off.py passes (73 passed with test_setup.py).
findings.summary: false lines derived from marketplace.json against a literal always-on list: a plugin rename the literal misses writes relay@amidman: false and silently turns the merge hook off

details: CONFIRMED by reading. Option B (line 89-95) makes the existing relay key the record of --product and --flow issues on an
existing project; section 7 (line 147-149) then claims the rename needs "no extra migration code" because the false
lines are derived. Only the false lines with no other source are derivable; the true lines kept under B are not. The
[plugin_key] table already maps old -> new, so the fix is small and inside the design: carry the old value to the new
key when the new key is absent, then apply rows 1-3. This also matches the rename item. Size: 10 design, 20 build.
evidence: lib/relay_old_names.toml [plugin_key]  "sdd@relay" = "openspec@relay" (an old -> new map, today used only to delete)
design line 89-95 (option B keeps existing keys), line 147-149 ("deleted through [plugin_key] ... no extra migration code")
queue the-core-plugin-becomes-relay-amidman What: "relay setup's migrate moves existing settings (enabledPlugins keys ...)"
failing_case: A Phoenix project set up with `relay setup <dir> --product` (detect() never sees lib/shop_web, the design's own outside
note), so its settings hold `product@relay: true` only because option B keeps it. After the rename, a plain
`relay setup <dir>`: [plugin_key] maps product@relay -> product@amidman and merge_settings (lib/relay_setup.py:336-339)
pops the old key; row 1 does not apply (d["ui"] False), row 4 finds no product@amidman key, row 5 writes
`product@amidman: false`. The look review is silently off. The same happens to an `issues@relay: true` that only
option B keeps (keys of other marketplaces are untouched and do not lose anything).
Should: product@amidman: true (the value moves to the new key, as the rename item says: "migrate moves existing settings").
fix_hint: Section 2 "kept as today" and section 7: an old key from [plugin_key] moves its value to the new key when the new key is
absent (then the table applies); add pass-case 1 as a test.
pass_cases: 1. Settings product@relay true, no ui marker, [plugin_key] product@relay -> product@amidman, plain run -> product@amidman true, no product@relay key.
2. Settings issues@relay false, mapped -> issues@amidman false.
3. Settings sdd@relay true with today's [plugin_key] (sdd@relay -> openspec@relay), [specs] none -> openspec@relay false (the spec row still decides).
4. No old key -> rows of the table as designed (T9).
reason: Carried from the earlier check of 5ecc184 (MET there); the only change since is the t22 test rewrite 8739ae9, and tests/test_setup_off.py passes (73 passed with test_setup.py).
findings.summary: section 7 says the rename deletes old X@relay keys and re-derives false, but under option B the kept values are data: a hand or --product true is lost

details: CONFIRMED by reading flag(). Every test in the design calls setup() directly (T1-T16), so a CLI that drops the second
flag passes all of them. Cheap to fix in the design: name a repeated-flag parse and one CLI test. Size: 5.
evidence: bin/relay:135-140  if name in args: i = args.index(name); value = args[i + 1]; del args[i:i + 2]; return value
bin/relay:393  root = os.path.realpath(args[0] if args else os.getcwd())   (leftover args never checked)
failing_case: `relay setup . --off a@m --off b@m` built with today's helper `flag(args, "--off")` (bin/relay:134-143): only a@m is
taken; "--off b@m" stays in args and cmd_setup never rejects leftovers, so b@m is silently not turned off.
Should: both a@m and b@m false, or a usage error.
fix_hint: Section 8: "--off is collected by a loop (all occurrences); leftover arguments starting with -- are a usage error"; add pass-case 1.
pass_cases: 1. CLI `relay setup <dir> --off a@m --off b@m --no-global` (both in the fixture registry) -> both keys false.
2. CLI with one --off -> as T1.
3. CLI `--off` with no value -> usage error, nothing written.
reason: Carried from the earlier check of 5ecc184 (MET there); the only change since is the t22 test rewrite 8739ae9, and tests/test_setup_off.py passes (73 passed with test_setup.py).

details: PLAUSIBLE as a design gap (traced by reading doctor; not run on relay). The queue item's point is that relay is the
first project that runs relay; a doctor that is red by design on relay teaches the reader to ignore it. Not a defect of
the off-plugins logic; the smallest answer is a line under "Not decided" or a queue item (relay's quiet check / gate keys).
Size: 5 in the design.
evidence: lib/relay_setup.py:1053-1055  for s in ("check", "ci", "wt"): path = cfg.get("gate", {}).get(s, f"bin/{s}"); ok(... os.path.isfile(path) ...)
failing_case: Relay tree after the design is built and T1 is applied: `relay doctor /Users/amidman/relay` reports FIX
"gate.check exists and is executable" (bin/check absent; kit.toml has no [gate], so the default bin/check is checked,
lib/relay_setup.py:1053-1055) and FIX "gate.wt exists" (no bin/wt). The design (line 122-126, 39-40) keeps both FIX
on purpose and says bin/ci cannot be gate.check. A later `core@relay is off` FIX shows as a third red line among two
that are always red.
Should: relay's doctor is green when relay is set up as designed, or the design names how it gets there.
fix_hint: Add to "Not decided": relay's doctor keeps gate.check and gate.wt FIX until relay has a quiet check and a worktree
script (or kit.toml names what relay uses); queue it as an item.
pass_cases: 1. Relay tree after T1: doctor's project part has no FIX (or the design lists the two FIX as accepted, with the item that clears them).
2. Folder with kit.toml and no bin/check (T10): doctor FIX as today.
reason: Carried from the earlier check of 5ecc184 (MET there); the only change since is the t22 test rewrite 8739ae9, and tests/test_setup_off.py passes (73 passed with test_setup.py).
findings.summary: relay, the first tester, keeps two permanent doctor FIX lines (gate.check, gate.wt), so the new always-on FIX lands among red lines nobody clears

details: PLAUSIBLE (traced by reading; not run, it would touch live files). The design's critique already notes sync runs (line
209-211) but the procedure's expected outcome does not. Size: 5.
evidence: bin/relay:421-425  results = relay_rules.sync(..., only={d["name"], "global"} if not no_global else {d["name"]}, ...); except Held: return 1
failing_case: `bin/relay setup . --off gopls-lsp@claude-plugins-official --no-global` in /Users/amidman/relay/.worktrees/relay-plugins:
after setup() writes settings.json, cmd_setup (bin/relay:421-425) calls relay_rules.sync(only={"relay"}) with ROOT =
the worktree; it renders /Users/amidman/relay/CLAUDE.local.md (projects.toml [relay] file) from the worktree's rules
(lib/relay_rules.py:37 builds paths from ROOT), or, when merges are waiting for a paid run, prints "Not synced" and
exits 1. Either way the run is not "settings.json and nothing else"; an exit 1 reads as a failed setup.
Should: the step names the expected sync outcome (untracked CLAUDE.local.md rewritten, or exit 1 held) as acceptable,
or runs after rules-rendered-from-a-linked-worktree-write-that lands.
fix_hint: Reword line 196-198: expected git diff is settings.json only; sync may rewrite the untracked CLAUDE.local.md or stop held (exit 1).
pass_cases: 1. The design's relay-plugins paragraph names: git diff = .claude/settings.json only; CLAUDE.local.md (ignored via .git/info/exclude) may be rewritten; exit 1 "Not synced" is not a setup failure.
reason: Carried from the earlier check of 5ecc184 (GAP there): relay sync from a linked worktree is not covered by this change; for the owner as recorded, unchanged by 8739ae9.
findings.summary: the relay-plugins step expects 'T1's settings.json and nothing else', but cmd_setup then runs relay sync from the linked worktree, which can rewrite CLAUDE.local.md or exit 1 when held
